scope: Controlled native Moebius diagnosis on the exact float context of the saved GFX painted fill; distinguish graph cache, incomplete committed selection and inference padding. No change to production sampling defaults or saved targets.

observations.native_reproduction: All 512×512×4 float samples exactly match the saved native EXR asset.
observations.partial_selection: The original 20473-pixel target is a narrow central strip and leaves visible parts of the head and arms outside it. Preserving those pixels prevents complete removal.
observations.portable_cache: Same pinned model/VAE hashes; changed float values are small (max 0.00189668, mean 0.00000445424 RGBA). A recognizable person remains; changing cache does not resolve this trial.
observations.wider_target: Explicit 32-pixel square dilation expands the target to 49604 pixels and removes the recognizable person on seed zero. Soft patch/brightness differences remain; no universal photographic-quality claim.
observations.inference_only: Inference padding 32 yields the exact same encoded inferred image as target padding 32, but committing through the old tight target preserves visible unselected remnants and a conspicuous narrow patch.
observations.additional_inference_padding: Adding 16 model pixels to the already wider target removes the person but produces a more visible wall/grass boundary in the inspected composition. No new default is justified.
observations.ui_guidance: Paint area now explains that the whole object, its edges and shadows must be covered, and that only painted pixels are replaced.

measurement_limits: One photo, one seed and 20 full-strength steps; qualitative inspection, not a model ranking or universal removal claim.
The wider target is an explicit diagnostic selection change, not automatic alteration of user paint or the XMP.
The final wider-target/padded-inference and PNG compatibility processes overlapped; their timings are integrity records and are not a latency comparison.
Parallel EXR compression can change file bytes without changing float pixels. Final records include a canonical float-buffer hash separately from the EXR file hash.
The PNG compatibility run has an input quantization round trip and is not the exact-float native reproduction.
